open_questions: High-resolution photometry/spectroscopy to test for a diluted neighbour eclipsing binary
Repeat TESS sectors to confirm stable depth
dossier.public_summary: The dip looks shallow and flat-bottomed at 2.5 Earth radii, but its apparent depth changes dramatically from sector to sector and even within the same pipeline (from ~1200 to ~5000 ppm), and the handful of individual transits disagree strongly. Together with an inconclusive position measurement, this neither matches a steady planet on the target nor can be saved by calibration, so the best explanation is not a planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes by factor >3 between sectors and both decreases and a 3.8x increase within TESS-SPOC alone. A planet on the target must have a constant depth; this requires a variable contaminant or spot crossings, favouring not a planet.
reasons.value: p_constant 0.000002124, verdict changes_within_a_source, per-sector depths 1321 +/- 425, 3469 +/- 436, 5055 +/- 659 ppm, depth_change_pct 113.8

reasons.why: Individual transit depths are inconsistent and a few deep outliers dominate the detection. Favors a few false events (noise/outliers) rather than a steady planet.
Cannot confirm the dip is on the target; the centroid test fails as expected for a weak/variable signal, removing the key counter-evidence against an off-target blended eclipsing binary.
